messages:
alex: Heads up — ran into a nasty import/typing mismatch when consuming the JS SDK from a webpack app that later gets bundled for edge via Vite. Named exports resolve at build but end up on `.default` at runtime.

priya: Interesting. Which bundler flow exactly? webpack -> SSR -> Vite?

alex: Our flow: app built with webpack for web, but we also produce a server-side bundle for edge that uses Vite (SSR) and esbuild. Locally `node` + CJS works. Production edge shows `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor` because `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` logs an object like `{ default: { RedwoodClient: [Function] } }`.

leo: Classic conditional exports / interop dance. Did you check package.json exports + module/main fields? If package only exposes CJS in some paths, Vite's optimizeDeps can pre-bundle the CJS and convert to ESM incorrectly.

alex: package.json has both but with a subtle conditional: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }. SDK's CJS uses `exports.RedwoodClient = RedwoodClient`, ESM uses `export class RedwoodClient {}` — still, transforms sometimes wrap the whole thing into default.

emily: For webpack you can control resolution order with `resolve.mainFields`. Example: `resolve: { mainFields: ['browser', 'module', 'main'] }` ensures webpack prefers ESM. For Vite, `ssr.noExternal` or `optimizeDeps.exclude` can help.

priya: Also check tsconfig/compilerOptions: `esModuleInterop` vs `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`. Consumer code compiled with `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true` may compile `import RedwoodClient from` into different runtime forms. Types mismatch shows up if you switch import shapes.

leo: Repro I used: tiny repro package that publishes a CJS-only tarball and an app that `type: module` + Vite SSR. Prebundle moves CJS -> ESM wrapper and the named export gets nested. Repro steps are short: publish test package locally, vite + ssr -> `console.log(require('@test/pkg'))` vs `import pkg from '@test/pkg'` shows different shapes.

alex: Workarounds that worked for us (app side):
- force using the ESM entry: `import('@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js')` (not ideal)
- in vite.config: `ssr: { noExternal: ['@redwood/inference'] }` to avoid prebundling the published CJS path
- webpack: ensure `mainFields` preference includes `module` before `main`

emily: Library-side fixes (what to ask SDK team to publish):
- publish a real named-export ESM entry and make sure it uses `export class RedwoodClient {}` (not default-only)
- include a `default` export that points to the same symbol (so consumers importing default or named both work)
- expand package.json exports to include an explicit `"types"` mapping for the import entry so TS follows the same path. Example snippet: `"exports": { ".": { "import": { "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts", "default": "./dist/esm/index.js" }, "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }`

priya: And add a tiny bundler smoke test in CI: run a minimal Vite SSR and a webpack bundle against the shipped package to catch regressions. A single node test that does `node --input-type=module 'console.log((await import("./dist/bundle.mjs")).RedwoodClient)'` is quick.

leo: Another library trick: ship index.js that re-exports both shapes:
```js
// dist/esm/index.js
export class RedwoodClient {}
export default { RedwoodClient }
```
That is ugly but makes both import flavors survive. Better: use build tool to generate `export { RedwoodClient } from './client.js'; export { default } from './client.js';` with proper interop helpers.

alex: Types were a thorn: consumers using `import RedwoodPkg from '@redwood/inference'` see `Module has no default export` unless d.ts includes `export default RedwoodClient;`. So recommend d.ts include both named and default.

emily: For webpack users, `module.exports.__esModule = true` in the CJS shim sometimes prevents the default-wrapping. TS + bundler teams should avoid relying on synthetic wrappers.

priya: Priors: Vite's optimizeDeps runs esbuild which aggressively converts CJS -> ESM. If the package exposes both, esbuild may prefer the CJS variant if the import path triggers it. `ssr.noExternal` is usually the fastest fix.

alex: I'll file an SDK issue with: repro (small repo), example failing bundle output, recommended package.json exports patch, and a suggestion to add bundler smoke tests. Will ping SDK maintainers.

devex-bot: Reminder: add the repro repo link to the issue and tag `sdk-maintainers` before merging.

leo: Quick app-side snippet if someone needs an immediate safe-import:```js
async function safeLoad() {
  const m = await import('@redwood/inference');
  return m.RedwoodClient || m.default?.RedwoodClient || m.default;
}
const RedwoodClient = await safeLoad();
```
Not great but stops crashes while SDK team fixes publishing.

emily: Thanks — this should help whoever lands the publish fix. :thumbsup:
